subject: Cobalt discovery — perf validation and bench plan
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cobalt discovery — perf validation and bench plan

Quick recap from the call with Asha/Ravi at Cobalt earlier today (30m):

TL;DR: Cobalt wants a head-to-head validation vs their current hyperscaler endpoint. Primary goals are p95 latency <= 120ms for typical prompt mix, p99 <= 300ms for heavier prompts, and sustained tokens/sec around 240–280 at 75% utilization. They emphasized consistency (low tail) over occasional best-case throughput.

What they shared:
- Prod-like prompts: mostly short-form dialogue + structured QA pairs, median prompt length ~ 45 tokens, 95th ~ 420 tokens.
- Expected concurrency: 40–60 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Current hyperscaler config: 8x A100 equivalent, batching enabled client-side, no KV cache.
- Success signals: p95/p99 reporting, tokens/sec, 5xx rate under 0.5%.

Immediate asks for Redwood:
1) Run an A/B perf run (Redwood hosted vs their hyperscaler endpoint) using Cobalt sample payloads + our synthetic edge cases (microbursts, long prompts).
2) Capture p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, tail queuing times, and failure modes for both runs.
3) Provide a short writeup with configuration differences and recommendations (e.g., batching, KV caching, quantization tradeoffs).

Attachments: I uploaded the sample payloads they shared to the drive (see link) and attached a copy to this thread (cobalt_payload_samples.jsonl).

Proposed internal owners / asks:
- Irene: lead the A/B test design and run. Suggest you confirm model variants we should test and which kernel/quantization configs to include.
- Karthik: help validate traffic shaping and synthetic microburst harness (we'll reuse the bench runner).
- Jordan: prepare the comparative slide deck for the customer debrief and call out cost/latency tradeoffs.

Timeline suggestion: start baseline runs next Tue (2028-06-20), run for 48–72h to capture diurnal variance, debrief Fri 2028-06-23. If that works, I’ll coordinate with Asha for whitelisting and any staging endpoint access.

Notes / constraints: they asked we not run aggressive scale tests against prod without permission. We'll request a staging endpoint and/or whitelisted IPs.

—Marcus
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Cobalt discovery — perf validation and bench plan

Thanks for the recap — I can take point on the A/B. High-level plan below; details in the attached internal-ab-test-proposal.md.

Summary of proposed A/B test design:
- Baselines:
  1) Cobalt hyperscaler endpoint (customer-provided) — the control
  2) Redwood Hosted (our standard RT config) — variant A
  3) Redwood Dedicated (quantized/optimized inference) — variant B (if customer allows longer-running jobs)
- Metrics captured: p50/p75/p95/p99 latency (generation start to final token), tokens/sec (per-GPU and aggregate), queue latency, CPU/GPU utilization, OOM/retries, 5xx/4xx rates.
- Test harness: bench-runner v2 (we'll reuse the sequence-preserving mode for KV cache tests). Scripts will replay cobalt_payload_samples.jsonl at target concurrency profiles (40/50/60), plus three microburst windows where qps spikes 3–5x for 30–60s.
- Model matrix: need confirmation from Marcus on target model(s). Suggest we test two flavors: a densest 1) open-llm-70b (float16), and 2) same model quantized (q4f/gamma) to show cost/latency tradeoffs. If Cobalt is using a different model, swap accordingly.
- Config knobs to sweep: batching window (1–30ms), max batch size, KV cache on/off, request streaming vs non-streaming.

Acceptance thresholds (for negotiation with customer):
- p95 <= 150ms for typical prompts (goal 120ms)
- p99 <= 350ms (goal 300ms)
- tokens/sec sustain >= 220 tokens/sec per 8-GPU cluster (adjusted once we see real concurrency)

Data & access requests from customer:
- Staging endpoint (or whitelisted IPs) to hit their endpoint for a direct control run
- Any rate limits/alerts we need to observe
- Clarify model name/version and whether they want redwood to stage model variants in their account (if doing Dedicated tests)

Timeline:
- Mon 6/19: finalize model matrix and scripts (internal)
- Tue 6/20: get staging access & run quick smoke tests
- Tue 6/20–Thu 6/22: 48–72h A/B runs
- Fri 6/23: internal debrief -> prep customer deck (Jordan)

I attached a short proposal with exact experiment steps and the bench config we plan to run. I’ll create a runbook with dashboards for p95/p99 + tokens/sec.

—Irene
Sr. Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference

Asha / Ravi — thanks again for the call. Per our discussion, Redwood will run a comparative perf validation vs your hyperscaler endpoint. High-level ask: can you share the staging endpoint + whitelist our test IPs for Tue 6/20 through Thu 6/22? Below is what we need from your side to run the control:

1) Staging API endpoint (URL) or a list of IPs to whitelist
2) Model name & version used in your current hyperscaler setup
3) Any rate limits we should respect when running the control runs
4) (Optional) A small sample of live production prompts (we received the initial sample — thank you) — if you can provide another 500 examples focused on long-form prompts, we’ll include those in the tail tests.

Planned customer-facing deliverables:
- A/B run artifacts (raw CSVs) + a summary deck that calls out: configuration differences, p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, estimated cost per 1M tokens under each config, and suggested ops recommendations (batching, caching, quantization).

We’ll run the Redwood side in parallel to the control. For transparency, we won’t stress your prod; we’ll hit staging or run with small bursts if needed.

Proposed dates (same as internal): Tue 6/20 — Thu 6/22, debrief Fri 6/23. Please confirm staging access and model version; I’ll share the whitelisting IPs once Irene confirms the runner.

Thanks — looking forward to moving fast on this.

—Marcus
